v0.7 acceptance additions
-------------------------
- LogRule may be registered atomically dormant with addDormantRule(), or via
  addRule(..., initiallyEnabled=.false). Validation and any exact scope crypto
  checks happen before publication, but disabled rules are omitted from the
  compiled method/class indexes.
- DORMANT_RUNTIME_ACTIVATION proves a lightweight object receives no proxy and
  the service has zero compiled plans while its incident rule is dormant.
- Arming that rule makes proxy creation eligible. A benign call through the
  active proxy evaluates one exact predicate but creates zero LogInvocation,
  active logger, or LogEvent objects.
- Disarming the rule removes the plan. New references get the original object,
  and an already-issued proxy performs zero plan evaluations and emits no stale
  events after disarm.
- LogRuntimeControl provides the narrow operational service/rule/target toggle
  surface. It does not expose rule definition/replacement APIs.
- LogControlEvent records control operation, subject, old/new state, reason and
  caller-supplied actorId as a structured object outside normal LogEvent
  delivery. actorId is provenance only, not a cryptographic-authority claim.
- The control journal is bounded (default 1024, constructor configurable) and
  exposes controlEventsDropped. CONTROL_JOURNAL_BOUND verifies a 3-entry
  service retains the newest 3 of 5 control changes and reports dropped=2.
- LogRuntimeSnapshot exposes structured service, rule, target, registration and
  compiled-plan status without adding observers/callbacks to the hot path.
- LogRuntimeNoSQLAdapter exposes fresh read-only object-table snapshots:
  runtime, rules, targets, registrations, plans, control_events.
- Runtime NoSQL raw values retain the actual LogService, LogRule, target,
  registration, plan and LogControlEvent objects. SQL-visible fields are only
  bounded projections.
- An executable UPDATE attempt against ctl_rules is NOTEXECUTED and cannot
  change the underlying LogRule, proving SQL inspection cannot bypass the
  coherent LogRuntimeControl path.

Core performance acceptance
---------------------------
The hard acceptance properties remain structural rather than timer based:
- with no applicable rule/target/policy, registered substantial-object methods
  are physically unwrapped and perform zero logging plan/predicate work;
- dormant lightweight rules create zero proxies and zero compiled plans;
- an armed selective condition miss creates zero invocation/logger/event
  objects;
- an already-issued lightweight proxy performs zero plan work after disarm;
- Institutional Policy deployment/topology resolution remains activation-time
  work and is not called from ordinary logged business invocations.

The supplied debug/internal-test interpreter was also sampled with 300,000
explicit sends to the singleton null logger. Three consecutive standalone
samples during v0.7 validation were 1.910, 2.046 and 2.068 microseconds of
incremental time per call. A full-suite sample under concurrent system load was
7.471 microseconds, illustrating why this microbenchmark is supporting evidence
rather than a portable acceptance threshold.

Existing integration floor retained
-----------------------------------
- Alchemy Objects v0.8 cooperative interposition in both installation orders;
- real crypto-locked method logging;
- exact cross-scope/domain Alchemy capability checks;
- Institutional Policy v0.6 publication, effective dating, progressive overlap,
  policy seal integrity and atomic handover;
- NoSQLServer structured event querying and raw object preservation;
- Queue Fabric direct, topic/subscriber, exact security-domain enforcement and
  durable event/0.4 object-graph persistence;
- executable recovery of event/0.3, event/0.2 and event/0.1 records.

Final artifact verification
---------------------------
The release candidate ZIP was extracted to a fresh directory. All 54 entries in
MANIFEST.sha256 verified successfully and the complete suite reran from that
extracted copy against the exact interpreter/dependency set above.

Clean-artifact acceptance highlights:

After recording this evidence, the package is resealed, its manifest regenerated,
and that final ZIP is extracted and rerun once more so the distributed checksum
corresponds to a tested artifact.
